answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the willow of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, revoked by a single upheld challenge, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. The karst holds work receipts rather than names, so the quartz of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread.
